title: Capturing an anchor return
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and choose Boolean parameters for the forwarding, find, and startup modes and a Boolean word $p$. Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, $c$ a configuration of $B$ on $x$, $r$ a release bit, $t$ a natural number, $w$ a Boolean word, and $u$ a configuration of $F$ on $x$. Suppose the run of $B$ from $c$ is in state $a$ at time $t$; if $t=0$, suppose $r$ is false; and at every time $v<t$, either $v=0$ and $r$ is true, or the run is not in state $a$. Then the loop host run for $t+1$ steps, started from the image of the padded body configuration formed from $c,r$, no flag, $w$, and $u$, equals the image of the padded configuration formed from the body run at time $t$ with its state set to halted, release false, and flag set to false, using the same modes, prefix, word, and fuel configuration.
hypotheses_covered: Forwarding, find, and startup parameters are Boolean
The body run from $c$ is in state $a$ at time $t$
At every $v<t$, either $v=0$ and $r$ is true, or the body run is not in state $a$
caveat: The conclusion compares configurations built by private image and padding constructions; the supplied informal definitions do not fully specify the image construction.
replaced:
Let $c$ be a body configuration, $t$ a time at which the body run from $c$ sits in the
anchor state, with no earlier anchor visit except possibly a released step at time zero,
and with the release bit clear whenever $t = 0$. Then the loop host, run for $t + 1$
steps from the body call built on $c$, reaches the stopped call whose body data is the
body run at time $t$ with control removed, release clear, and stop flag
$\mathrm{false}$, with the counter word and fuel residue unchanged.
